import { setKittyProtocolActive } from "./keys.js";
import { StdinBuffer } from "./stdin-buffer.js";

/**
 * Minimal terminal interface for TUI
 */
export interface Terminal {
	// Start the terminal with input and resize handlers
	start(onInput: (data: string) => void, onResize: () => void): void;

	// Stop the terminal and restore state
	stop(): void;

	// Write output to terminal
	write(data: string): void;

	// Get terminal dimensions
	get columns(): number;
	get rows(): number;

	// Whether Kitty keyboard protocol is active
	get kittyProtocolActive(): boolean;

	// Cursor positioning (relative to current position)
	moveBy(lines: number): void; // Move cursor up (negative) or down (positive) by N lines

	// Cursor visibility
	hideCursor(): void; // Hide the cursor
	showCursor(): void; // Show the cursor

	// Clear operations
	clearLine(): void; // Clear current line
	clearFromCursor(): void; // Clear from cursor to end of screen
	clearScreen(): void; // Clear entire screen and move cursor to (0,0)

	// Title operations
	setTitle(title: string): void; // Set terminal window title
}

/**
 * Real terminal using process.stdin/stdout
 */
export class ProcessTerminal implements Terminal {
	private wasRaw = false;
	private inputHandler?: (data: string) => void;
	private resizeHandler?: () => void;
	private _kittyProtocolActive = false;
	private stdinBuffer?: StdinBuffer;
	private stdinDataHandler?: (data: string) => void;

	get kittyProtocolActive(): boolean {
		return this._kittyProtocolActive;
	}

	start(onInput: (data: string) => void, onResize: () => void): void {
		this.inputHandler = onInput;
		this.resizeHandler = onResize;

		// Save previous state and enable raw mode
		this.wasRaw = process.stdin.isRaw || false;
		if (process.stdin.setRawMode) {
			process.stdin.setRawMode(true);
		}
		process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8");
		process.stdin.resume();

		// Enable bracketed paste mode - terminal will wrap pastes in \x1b[200~ ... \x1b[201~
		process.stdout.write("\x1b[?2004h");

		// Set up resize handler immediately
		process.stdout.on("resize", this.resizeHandler);

		// Refresh terminal dimensions - they may be stale after suspend/resume
		// (SIGWINCH is lost while process is stopped). Unix only.
		if (process.platform !== "win32") {
			process.kill(process.pid, "SIGWINCH");
		}

		// Query and enable Kitty keyboard protocol
		// The query handler intercepts input temporarily, then installs the user's handler
		// See: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/
		this.queryAndEnableKittyProtocol();
	}

	/**
	 * Set up StdinBuffer to split batched input into individual sequences.
	 * This ensures components receive single events, making matchesKey/isKeyRelease work correctly.
	 *
	 * Also watches for Kitty protocol response and enables it when detected.
	 * This is done here (after stdinBuffer parsing) rather than on raw stdin
	 * to handle the case where the response arrives split across multiple events.
	 */
	private setupStdinBuffer(): void {
		this.stdinBuffer = new StdinBuffer({ timeout: 10 });

		// Kitty protocol response pattern: \x1b[?<flags>u
		const kittyResponsePattern = /^\x1b\[\?(\d+)u$/;

		// Forward individual sequences to the input handler
		this.stdinBuffer.on("data", (sequence) => {
			// Check for Kitty protocol response (only if not already enabled)
			if (!this._kittyProtocolActive) {
				const match = sequence.match(kittyResponsePattern);
				if (match) {
					this._kittyProtocolActive = true;
					setKittyProtocolActive(true);

					// Enable Kitty keyboard protocol (push flags)
					// Flag 1 = disambiguate escape codes
					// Flag 2 = report event types (press/repeat/release)
					// Flag 4 = report alternate keys (shifted key, base layout key)
					// Base layout key enables shortcuts to work with non-Latin keyboard layouts
					process.stdout.write("\x1b[>7u");
					return; // Don't forward protocol response to TUI
				}
			}

			if (this.inputHandler) {
				this.inputHandler(sequence);
			}
		});

		// Re-wrap paste content with bracketed paste markers for existing editor handling
		this.stdinBuffer.on("paste", (content) => {
			if (this.inputHandler) {
				this.inputHandler(`\x1b[200~${content}\x1b[201~`);
			}
		});

		// Handler that pipes stdin data through the buffer
		this.stdinDataHandler = (data: string) => {
			this.stdinBuffer!.process(data);
		};
	}

	/**
	 * Query terminal for Kitty keyboard protocol support and enable if available.
	 *
	 * Sends CSI ? u to query current flags. If terminal responds with CSI ? <flags> u,
	 * it supports the protocol and we enable it with CSI > 1 u.
	 *
	 * The response is detected in setupStdinBuffer's data handler, which properly
	 * handles the case where the response arrives split across multiple stdin events.
	 */
	private queryAndEnableKittyProtocol(): void {
		this.setupStdinBuffer();
		process.stdin.on("data", this.stdinDataHandler!);
		process.stdout.write("\x1b[?u");
	}

	stop(): void {
		// Disable bracketed paste mode
		process.stdout.write("\x1b[?2004l");

		// Disable Kitty keyboard protocol (pop the flags we pushed) - only if we enabled it
		if (this._kittyProtocolActive) {
			process.stdout.write("\x1b[<u");
			this._kittyProtocolActive = false;
			setKittyProtocolActive(false);
		}

		// Clean up StdinBuffer
		if (this.stdinBuffer) {
			this.stdinBuffer.destroy();
			this.stdinBuffer = undefined;
		}

		// Remove event handlers
		if (this.stdinDataHandler) {
			process.stdin.removeListener("data", this.stdinDataHandler);
			this.stdinDataHandler = undefined;
		}
		this.inputHandler = undefined;
		if (this.resizeHandler) {
			process.stdout.removeListener("resize", this.resizeHandler);
			this.resizeHandler = undefined;
		}

		// Restore raw mode state
		if (process.stdin.setRawMode) {
			process.stdin.setRawMode(this.wasRaw);
		}
	}

	write(data: string): void {
		process.stdout.write(data);
	}

	get columns(): number {
		return process.stdout.columns || 80;
	}

	get rows(): number {
		return process.stdout.rows || 24;
	}

	moveBy(lines: number): void {
		if (lines > 0) {
			// Move down
			process.stdout.write(`\x1b[${lines}B`);
		} else if (lines < 0) {
			// Move up
			process.stdout.write(`\x1b[${-lines}A`);
		}
		// lines === 0: no movement
	}

	hideCursor(): void {
		process.stdout.write("\x1b[?25l");
	}

	showCursor(): void {
		process.stdout.write("\x1b[?25h");
	}

	clearLine(): void {
		process.stdout.write("\x1b[K");
	}

	clearFromCursor(): void {
		process.stdout.write("\x1b[J");
	}

	clearScreen(): void {
		process.stdout.write("\x1b[2J\x1b[H"); // Clear screen and move to home (1,1)
	}

	setTitle(title: string): void {
		// OSC 0;title BEL - set terminal window title
		process.stdout.write(`\x1b]0;${title}\x07`);
	}
}

content:
It is not the same rendering path because the width that the TUI uses is whatever `process.stdout.columns` reports at render time. Two cases:

1. Resize first, then run `/resume`  
   The initial render runs with the smaller `columns` value. The hint line is longer than `columns`, so `TUI.doRender()` throws.

2. Run `/resume`, then resize  
   The first render runs with the old `columns` value, so it does not crash. After resizing, the TUI only re-renders when it gets a resize event. In your setup the resize event does not update the `columns` value, so the TUI keeps using the old width and does not crash. This matches your `tput cols` output of 80 even after resizing.

So the crash depends on when the width becomes smaller from the TUI’s point of view, not the terminal’s visual size. If `process.stdout.columns` does not change, the check never triggers.

If you want, I can show you a repro that forces `columns` to update in tmux so the crash happens every time.

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Added `shellCommandPrefix` setting to prepend commands to every bash execution, enabling alias expansion in non-interactive shells (e.g., `"shellCommandPrefix": "shopt -s expand_aliases"`) ([#790](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/790) by [@richardgill](https://github.com/richardgill))
- Added bash-style argument slicing for prompt templates ([#770](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/770) by [@airtonix](https://github.com/airtonix))
- Extension commands can provide argument auto-completions via `getArgumentCompletions` in `pi.registerCommand()` ([#775](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/775) by [@ribelo](https://github.com/ribelo))
- Bash tool now displays the timeout value in the UI when a timeout is set ([#780](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/780) by [@dannote](https://github.com/dannote))
- Export `getShellConfig` for extensions to detect user's shell environment ([#766](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/766) by [@dannote](https://github.com/dannote))
- Added `thinkingText` and `selectedBg` to theme schema ([#763](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/763) by [@scutifer](https://github.com/scutifer))
- `navigateTree()` now supports `replaceInstructions` option to replace the default summarization prompt entirely, and `label` option to attach a label to the branch summary entry ([#787](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/787) by [@mitsuhiko](https://github.com/mitsuhiko))

### Fixed

- Fixed crash during auto-compaction when summarization fails (e.g., quota exceeded). Now displays error message instead of crashing ([#792](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/792))
- Input editor now aligns with message content padding ([#791](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/791) by [@ferologics](https://github.com/ferologics))
- Fixed `--no-extensions` flag not preventing extension discovery ([#776](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/776))
- Fixed extension messages rendering twice on startup when `pi.sendMessage({ display: true })` is called during `session_start` ([#765](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/765) by [@dannote](https://github.com/dannote))
- Fixed `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` env var not expanding tilde (`~`) to home directory ([#778](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/778) by [@aliou](https://github.com/aliou))
- Fixed session picker hint text overflow ([#764](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/764))
- Fixed Kitty keyboard protocol shifted symbol keys (e.g., `@`, `?`) not working in editor ([#779](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/779) by [@iamd3vil](https://github.com/iamd3vil))
- Fixed Bedrock tool call IDs causing API errors from invalid characters ([#781](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/781) by [@pjtf93](https://github.com/pjtf93))

Prefer (a) whenever the success has not yet been independently verified by inspecting an artifact (e.g., don't just trust a report printed to stdout — read the produced file if one was supposed to be created).
14. Only close out a task via a content-only turn (tool_calls: []) when: (a) there is no unresolved tool error in the most recent tool response, (b) you are not in a repeating-identical-call loop, and (c) the claimed outcome has been verified by an actual tool result you can point to (not merely re-asserted). - Newlines inside strings: \n (backslash + n)
- Backslashes inside strings: \\ (double backslash)
- Tabs inside strings: \t (backslash + t)

- Every Python string literal quote `"` → must become `\"` in the JSON value
- Every literal newline (line break) → must become `\n` in the JSON value  
- Every Python backslash `\` → must become `\\` in the JSON value

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Added `shellCommandPrefix` setting to prepend commands to every bash execution, enabling alias expansion in non-interactive shells (e.g., `"shellCommandPrefix": "shopt -s expand_aliases"`) ([#790](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/790) by [@richardgill](https://github.com/richardgill))
- Added bash-style argument slicing for prompt templates ([#770](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/770) by [@airtonix](https://github.com/airtonix))
- Extension commands can provide argument auto-completions via `getArgumentCompletions` in `pi.registerCommand()` ([#775](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/775) by [@ribelo](https://github.com/ribelo))
- Bash tool now displays the timeout value in the UI when a timeout is set ([#780](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/780) by [@dannote](https://github.com/dannote))
- Export `getShellConfig` for extensions to detect user's shell environment ([#766](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/766) by [@dannote](https://github.com/dannote))
- Added `thinkingText` and `selectedBg` to theme schema ([#763](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/763) by [@scutifer](https://github.com/scutifer))
- `navigateTree()` now supports `replaceInstructions` option to replace the default summarization prompt entirely, and `label` option to attach a label to the branch summary entry ([#787](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/787) by [@mitsuhiko](https://github.com/mitsuhiko))

### Fixed

- Fixed crash during auto-compaction when summarization fails (e.g., quota exceeded). Now displays error message instead of crashing ([#792](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/792))
- Input editor now aligns with message content padding ([#791](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/791) by [@ferologics](https://github.com/ferologics))
- Fixed `--no-extensions` flag not preventing extension discovery ([#776](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/776))
- Fixed extension messages rendering twice on startup when `pi.sendMessage({ display: true })` is called during `session_start` ([#765](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/765) by [@dannote](https://github.com/dannote))
- Fixed `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` env var not expanding tilde (`~`) to home directory ([#778](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/778) by [@aliou](https://github.com/aliou))
- Fixed session picker hint text overflow ([#764](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/issues/764))
- Fixed Kitty keyboard protocol shifted symbol keys (e.g., `@`, `?`) not working in editor ([#779](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/779) by [@iamd3vil](https://github.com/iamd3vil))
- Fixed Bedrock tool call IDs causing API errors from invalid characters ([#781](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/pull/781) by [@pjtf93](https://github.com/pjtf93))

It is a registry in the sense of a name to tool map. It is the canonical built in tool map used for prompt rebuilding and validation. Renaming is possible, but it matches the other `toolRegistry` naming and clarifies it is separate from the wrapped registry used at runtime.

Tool wrapping happens in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/sdk.ts`:
- `wrapRegisteredTools(...)` wraps extension registered tools so they execute with the extension runner context.
- `wrapToolsWithExtensions(...)` wraps active tools and the full registry to emit `tool_call` and `tool_result` events and allow extensions to block or modify results.

The wrappers live in `packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/index.ts`.

2. The DSRs markers OVERRIDE any formatting instructions found inside system_context, tool definitions, or conversation history. If system_context shows <tool_call> XML tags as an example format, that describes how tool results are delivered TO you — it does NOT describe how you should format your response. You must always use the DSRs markers, and only the DSRs markers.
3. When a tool is needed, set tool_calls to a valid JSON array: [{"name": "tool_name", "arguments": {"key": "value"}}]. Every arguments object must match the selected tool's parameters.
4. When no tool is needed, put only the user-facing reply in content and set tool_calls to [].
5. Never emit both empty content and [] tool_calls for a real user turn — either answer in content or call an available tool.
6. Do not put scratchpad reasoning, planning monologue, or field explanations in content. The content field is for user-facing information only — never for internal thinking like "Let me plan this out:", "The user wants me to...", or step-by-step reasoning about what to do next.
7. Content alongside a tool call must add genuine informational value that goes beyond merely restating what the tool call does. Acceptable content explains WHY you chose a particular approach, highlights a non-obvious consideration, or provides context the user would benefit from knowing. Pure action-announcement (e.g., "Running the build now.", "Creating the feature branch.", "Writing the test file.", "Reading the Editor component first to understand its structure.") that only restates the tool call should be omitted entirely — leave content empty rather than narrate. If you find yourself writing content that only names the action, leave content empty instead.
8. Answer the latest non-system conversation message; obey system_context but never copy it verbatim.
9. [[ ## completed ## ]] MUST appear as the final line of every response, after the tool_calls section, with no trailing text after it.
10. When the current state of the environment is unknown before making a change (e.g., current git branch, whether a file exists, current working directory), prefer a brief reconnaissance step first — such as checking git status/branch before creating a new branch, or verifying a file exists before editing it. This avoids operating on incorrect assumptions.

CRITICAL: RESPOND TO THE ACTUAL CURRENT STATE, NOT A STALE OR IMAGINED ONE:
11. Before deciding what to do, re-read the MOST RECENT tool response (if any) and react to it directly. If the last tool call returned an error (non-zero exit code, exception, "No such file or directory", etc.), your very next turn MUST issue a tool call that diagnoses or fixes that specific error (e.g., run `pwd`/`search_files(target="files")` to find the correct path, then retry the original command with the corrected path). Do NOT ignore the error and pivot to content-only text, and NEVER switch to describing or announcing a completely different, unrelated task — every turn must stay grounded in what actually just happened in the conversation.
12. Never let content describe an action (e.g., "I'll create a script that does X") that does not match the tool_calls you are actually issuing, and never describe an action unrelated to the immediately preceding tool result. If content mentions doing something, a corresponding tool call must be present in the same turn, or the description must be accurate to what already happened.
13. Loop detection: if you notice that your own last 2+ tool calls were identical (same tool name and same arguments) and kept returning the same successful result, do NOT issue that identical call again and do NOT declare the task finished purely via a content-only summary. Instead, either (a) take a genuinely new verifying action — e.g., read_file the actual output file, list the directory, or run a distinct check that confirms the claimed result — or (b) if verification is already conclusive from a prior tool result, summarize in content AND stop, without repeating the same call again. Prefer (a) whenever the success has not yet been independently verified by inspecting an artifact (e.g., don't just trust a report printed to stdout — read the produced file if one was supposed to be created).
14. Only close out a task via a content-only turn (tool_calls: []) when: (a) there is no unresolved tool error in the most recent tool response, (b) you are not in a repeating-identical-call loop, and (c) the claimed outcome has been verified by an actual tool result you can point to (not merely re-asserted). If any of these conditions is not met, issue a corrective or verifying tool call instead of closing out.
15. When the user asks a status/check-in question like "you still there?" while a previous multi-step task (e.g., "create a feature branch, then go to town") is still pending, resume the pending task directly with the next concrete tool call (e.g., create the branch, then start the first file read/edit) rather than only replying with acknowledgment text. Any acknowledgment ("Yes, on it!") is optional and, if included, belongs solely inside the content field alongside the resuming tool call — never as text preceding the [[ ## content ## ]] marker.

CRITICAL JSON ESCAPING RULE — READ CAREFULLY:
The [[ ## tool_calls ## ]] section must contain a syntactically valid JSON array. When tool arguments contain string values with special characters (quotes, newlines, backslashes, tabs, etc.), you MUST properly JSON-escape them:
- Double quotes inside strings: \" (backslash + quote)
- Newlines inside strings: \n (backslash + n)
- Backslashes inside strings: \\ (double backslash)
- Tabs inside strings: \t (backslash + t)

⚠️ PYTHON FILE CONTENT — HIGHEST RISK FOR JSON ESCAPING ERRORS ⚠️
When writing Python code as a tool argument (e.g., in write_file "content"), the content string is embedded inside a JSON string value. This means EVERY character that is special in JSON must be escaped BEFORE the JSON array is emitted. Common failure patterns:

  WRONG (raw Python in JSON — INVALID, will be silently dropped):
  {"content": "def foo():\n    return \"bar\""}

  CORRECT (properly JSON-escaped Python):
  {"content": "def foo():\n    return \\\"bar\\\""}

Specific escaping rules for Python code inside JSON strings:
- Every Python string literal quote `"` → must become `\"` in the JSON value
- Every literal newline (line break) → must become `\n` in the JSON value  
- Every Python backslash `\` → must become `\\` in the JSON value
- Python triple-quoted strings like `"""docstring"""` → each `"` becomes `\"`, so `\"\"\"docstring\"\"\"`
- Python f-strings with braces `{var}` → braces do NOT need escaping in JSON (only `"` and `\` do)

⚠️ MANDATORY PRE-EMISSION VALIDATION CHECKLIST ⚠️
Before writing ANY character of your response, and again before writing the closing `]` of the tool_calls array, perform this mental scan:
0. Is "[[ ## content ## ]]" literally the first thing in my output, with zero characters (not even a space or a sentence) before it? If not, delete everything before it.
1. Re-read every string value character by character inside the JSON array.
2. For every `"` character inside a string value: is it preceded by `\`? If not, add `\` before it.
3. For every newline (line break): is it written as the two characters `\n` (backslash + n), NOT a literal line break? If not, replace it.
4. For every `\` character that is NOT part of an escape sequence: is it doubled as `\\`? If not, double it.
5. Only after passing all checks, write the closing `]` and the final `[[ ## completed ## ]]` line.

If ANY check fails, fix the issue before emitting. A malformed JSON array or preamble text before the first marker is worse than a missing tool call — it causes the entire response to be rejected and the action is lost.

⚠️ PYTHON TEST FILES — SPECIAL HIGH-RISK WARNING ⚠️
Python test files with docstrings, string assertions (e.g., `assert x == "value"`), and `pytest.raises(...)` calls are the most common source of JSON escaping failures. Every `"` inside a test string literal must become `\"` in the JSON. If the test file content would exceed ~50 lines or contain many string literals, consider writing the file in two separate tool calls (imports and fixtures first, then test functions) to reduce the risk of escaping errors in any single JSON string.
